cards.explanation: The answer is that the LORD sees a dishonest scale as an abomination. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king (Proverbs 1:1), writes, “Dishonest scales are an abomination to the LORD…” Shaving a few crumbs off every sale might feel tiny, but the verse doesn't treat it that way. He's serious about honest dealing, friends.

The answer is delight. The second half of the verse says, “…but an accurate weight is His delight.” Same scale, same counter, and a whole different reaction from the LORD. An honest weight makes Him glad, friends.

The answer is disgrace. The proverb says, “When pride comes, disgrace follows…” Pride walks in first and disgrace shows up right behind it, no invitation needed. I've learned that a puffed-up chest and a quick fall go together.
The answer is True. Solomon says, “…but with humility comes wisdom.” Pride gets disgrace, and humility gets wisdom. I'd say that's a pretty good trade, friends.
The answer is their integrity. The verse says, “The integrity of the upright guides them…” It's like an inner compass that doesn't need batteries. The upright follow what's honest and whole in them.

The answer is their own perversity. The verse says, “…but the perversity of the faithless destroys them.” Integrity guides the upright, and perversity wrecks the faithless. They're taken down by their own twisted ways, friends.

The answer is righteousness. The verse says, “…but righteousness brings deliverance from death.” The first half says riches are worthless in the day of wrath. So money can't buy a way out, but righteousness brings one.
The answer is False. The verse says, “…but the wicked fall by their own wickedness.” It names their own wickedness, friends, and it says nothing about someone else tripping them.

The answer is desires. The verse says, “The righteousness of the upright delivers them, but the faithless are trapped by their own desires.” The upright are delivered by their righteousness. The faithless are trapped by their own desires.

The answer is False. Solomon says, “The righteous man is delivered from trouble; in his place the wicked man goes in.” The righteous man is delivered, and the wicked man takes his place in the trouble, friends.

The answer is knowledge. The verse says, “…but through knowledge the righteous are rescued.” The ungodly man uses his mouth to tear a neighbor down. The righteous are rescued through knowledge, friends.

The answer is the blessing of the upright. The verse says, “By the blessing of the upright a city is built up…” The wicked tear a city down with their mouths, and the upright build it up with a blessing. Words can do either one, friends.

The answer is True. The verse ends, “…but a man of understanding remains silent.” It sits right next to the line about showing contempt for a neighbor, which Solomon says lacks judgment. Sometimes the wise move is a closed mouth.

The answer is confidence. The verse says, “A gossip reveals a secret, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.” A secret handed to a trustworthy person stays safe. A gossip hands it to the next person, friends.

The answer is many counselors. The verse says, “…but with many counselors comes deliverance.” A nation with no guidance falls, and a nation with plenty of counselors is delivered. More good voices help it stand, friends.

The answer is secure. The verse says, “He who puts up security for a stranger will surely suffer, but the one who hates indebtedness is secure.” One will surely suffer. The one who hates indebtedness is secure, friends.

The answer is honor. The verse says, “A gracious woman attains honor, but ruthless men gain only wealth.” Both walk off with something, but it's not the same something. Honor is not something ruthless men get.

The answer is himself. Here's the twist, friends. The verse says, “A kind man benefits himself, but a cruel man brings trouble on himself.” The kind man is the one who benefits. The cruel man brings trouble on himself.

The answer is sows. The verse says, “…but he who sows righteousness reaps a true reward.” Sowing is planting, and what you plant comes up later. The wicked man earns an empty wage, and the one who sows righteousness reaps a true reward, friends.

The answer is False. The verse says, “Genuine righteousness leads to life, but the pursuit of evil brings death.” Genuine righteousness leads to life. The pursuit of evil brings death, friends, so it doesn't lead to life.

The answer is the blameless in their walk. The verse says, “…but the blameless in their walk are His delight.” It's the same word delight as the honest weight back in verse 1. The LORD is glad over those who walk blamelessly.
The answer is escape. The verse says, “…but the offspring of the righteous will escape.” The first half says the wicked will not go unpunished. The offspring of the righteous will escape, friends.

The answer is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion. The verse says, “Like a gold ring in a pig’s snout is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.” Gold is fine, but it looks out of place where it doesn't fit. I think Solomon is saying beauty without discretion sits oddly.
The answer is True. The verse says, “The desire of the righteous leads only to good…” Only good, friends, no side trips. The other half says the hope of the wicked brings wrath.

The answer is that he becomes poor. The verse says, “One gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds what is right, only to become poor.” Two people are set side by side. The one who gives freely gains even more, and the one who withholds what is right becomes poor, friends.
The answer is False. The verse says, “A generous soul will prosper, and he who refreshes others will himself be refreshed.” The one who refreshes others gets refreshed too, friends.

The answer is curse. The verse says, “The people will curse the hoarder of grain…” The grain is the same either way, but the town knows what the hoarder did. The one who sells it gets a blessing instead, friends.

The answer is that he will fall. The verse says, “He who trusts in his riches will fall…” Money makes a wobbly place to stand. Solomon also said riches are worthless in the day of wrath, back in verse 4.

The answer is True. The verse says, “…but the righteous will thrive like foliage.” Leaves are what a healthy plant shows off, and the righteous thrive in the same way. The man who trusts in his riches falls, and the righteous thrive, friends.

The answer is servant to the wise of heart. The verse says, “…and the fool will be servant to the wise of heart.” Whoever brings trouble on his house inherits the wind, and the fool ends up serving the wise of heart. That's quite a turn, friends.
The answer is wise. The verse says, “The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise.” The word is wise, friends, not rich or famous.
